question_text: Three processes arrive at time 0 in the order P1, P2, P3. Their CPU burst times are P1 = 8 ms, P2 = 4 ms and P3 = 2 ms. Ignore context-switch time. A process's waiting time is its completion time minus its burst time. Calculate the average waiting time when the processes are scheduled using: (i) first-come first-served (FCFS); (ii) round robin (RR) with a time quantum of 2 ms, where the ready queue starts in the order P1, P2, P3 and a pre-empted process rejoins the back of the queue.
adaptation_rationale: Original question written by Claude (single-agent Chunk 3 continuation, 2026-11-04) for a syllabus statement with no linked question at handover; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.
solution: (i) FCFS: P1 runs 0-8, P2 8-12, P3 12-14. Waiting times 0, 8, 12; average 20/3 = 6.67 ms. (ii) RR: P1 0-2, P2 2-4, P3 4-6 (finishes), P1 6-8, P2 8-10 (finishes), P1 10-14 (finishes at 14). Waiting times P1 14-8 = 6, P2 10-4 = 6, P3 6-2 = 4; average 16/3 = 5.33 ms.

marking_points.criterion: FCFS individual waiting times 0, 8 and 12 ms (or completion times 8, 12, 14).
RR completion times P3 = 6, P2 = 10, P1 = 14 ms shown by a valid timeline.

acceptable_alternatives: Accept 6.7 / 5.3 or exact fractions. Award average marks on follow-through from stated individual times.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 4 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.scope: Does not cover multilevel queue or priority scheduling; see O-C3-A-004. Context-switch overhead deliberately ignored and stated.
